s04FD24.name: Overworld sprites 9 and 10: drifting movement
summary: Main routines for overworld sprite types 9 ($04FD24) and 10 ($04FD70) in the OWSprites pointer table. Neither is named here (purpose unclear).
Each applies speed to position, draws one tile with X flip following X speed, then makes each speed swing between +/- limits:
every axis adds +1/-1 per step (DATA_04FD10) and reverses at the limit in DATA_04FD1A. Type 9 steps every second frame.
Type 10 steps X, Y and Z at different rates via masks DATA_04FD0A against a phase counter [$0E25], and is hidden (Y position forced off-screen) on some submaps.
Parameters: X = sprite slot [$0DDE]. Speed at [$0E95+$10*axis,X], direction index at [$0DF5+$10*axis,X].

s04FE00.name: Overworld sprite helpers: draw, move, home in
summary: $04FE00: draws a two-tile mirrored sprite whose tile size and X spacing depend on the Z height. Carry on entry = 16x16 flag.
$04FE4E: [$02] += Z height. $04FE5B: A = [$13] + DATA_04F833[X]. $04FE62: screen X in [$00], screen Y minus height in [$02].
$04FE90: apply X/Y/Z speeds to positions (Z clamped at 0). $04FEAB: one axis, speed in 1/16 pixel per frame, fraction in [$0EC5,X].
$04FED7: sets [$0EF7] = slot if the sprite is within 8 pixels of the player's map position. $04FEEF: dx, dy, |dx|, |dy| to the player.
$04FF2E: sets X/Y/Z speed to head toward the player (longest axis $20, others scaled); at the target zeroes speeds and Z height = $40.
